title: Data import: no way to write a column only when the row is created (re-running an upsert reverts state written since)
body:
## Context

hotsrm (an SRM app built purely from metadata) migrates legacy suppliers with the platform import (`POST /data/:object/import`, `writeMode: 'upsert'`). Migrations are run more than once (rehearsal, corrections), so the import must be idempotent: a re-run may refresh master-data columns, but it must **not** overwrite fields that the app's own flows or users have changed since the first run.

Example: legacy suppliers are created with `status = qualified` and `legacy_imported = true`. Between two runs a supplier gets frozen (`status = frozen`) and reviewed. A second upsert that carries the same `status` column silently moves it back to `qualified` (the state machine allows `frozen → qualified`), and `treatAsHistorical` is system-only anyway, so a signed-in admin cannot even send the first-run status through the import door.

## Gap

`ImportRequest` has `insert` / `update` / `upsert`, but nothing between them:

- no "create missing rows, skip existing ones" mode (`insert` has no match step, so re-runs fail with duplicate-key errors instead of reporting `skipped`);
- no per-column "on create only" flag in `FieldMappingEntry` (like `defaultValue` but applied only when the row is inserted).

## Proposal (either would do)

1. `writeMode: 'insert_missing'` (or `upsert` + `onExisting: 'skip'`): match on `matchFields`, report existing rows as `skipped`, create the rest.
2. `FieldMappingEntry.applyOn: 'create' | 'always'` (default `always`), so one sheet can carry "initial" columns that an update ignores.

## Workaround in hotsrm (temporary)

- `status.defaultValue = cel\`has(record.legacy_imported) && record.legacy_imported == true ? 'qualified' : 'potential'\`` so the sheet never carries `status`;
- `legacy_imported.readonlyWhen = previous.legacy_imported != true` so a re-run cannot mark an existing supplier;
- `initialStates` widened to include `qualified`, guarded by an insert-only script rule.

It works, but it spreads one import rule over three field declarations and is easy to get wrong (an expression default reading a field declared after it evaluates against an unset key unless guarded with `has()`).

Linked: objectstack-ai/hotsrm#10
